title: Microclient Onramp: chefbook notes and quicklab heuristics
body:
TL;DR: compact, opinionated onramp for embedding Redwood clients into microservices. Goal is a 10–15 minute dev loop: local smoke -> sandbox quicklab -> feature flag rollout. Focus telemetry-first: minimal contract, default dashboards, simple alerts.

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing long integration cycles for small services (2–4 engineers) that want an embedding/generation client in their stack. Friction: env var setup, non-obvious retry semantics, token accounting, and lack of clear telemetry to verify cost/latency.
- This doc is a living scratchbook: experiment notes for a tiny starter kit ("chefbook") that we can hand to product teams or solutions engineers. Not a final playbook, but enough to prototype and iterate.

Audience:
- Backend engineers integrating Redwood into microservices (REST/gRPC).
- Solutions/SEs doing 1:many pilots.
- Developer advocates building quicklabs.

One-line success metric:
- First meaningful request observed in telemetry within 15 minutes of handing starter kit to engineer.

Minimal quicklab flow (3 steps):
1) local: run docker-compose devkit (stubbed keys, local LRU cache) -> healthcheck + smoke prompt -> expect 200 + sample tokens.
2) sandbox: flip to sandbox API key, enable telemetry forwarded to dev team dashboard -> run 100 synthetic requests (latency distribution).
3) feature flag rollout: stage -> canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on token cost/latency regressions.

Artifacts included in chefbook (minimal):
- repo scaffold (README, example service, integration test)
- docker-compose/devkit with mocked upstream and sample prompts
- sample env file (.env.example) + short checklist
- telemetry contract (simple JSON lines headers) + example Grafana/Console dashboard link
- failure-mode cheat sheet (timeouts, backpressure, partial responses)

Telemetry contract (opinionated, small):
- Required fields per request event (JSON lines): request_id, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, http_status, error_code (optional), service_commit, env (local|sandbox|stg|prod).
- Aggregates exported: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens-per-request avg, error-rate, throttles, cost-per-route estimate.
- Default retention: 30d for detailed logs, 90d for aggregates (configurable).

Sample env (cookbook):
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood-sandbox-xxxx
- REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-embed-small-v1
- REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox
- REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_URL=https://ingest.telemetry.redwood.ai/devexp/microkit
- CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS=10000

Smoke tests (local):
- health: GET /_health -> checks env vars, cache, and ability to reach local stub (exit non-zero if fail).
- generation smoke: POST /generate with short prompt -> expect status 200 and token_count > 0.
- telemetry emit: run a short trace with metadata and verify line received on /events endpoint of devkit.

Failure scenarios and heuristics: 
- Upstream throttling: return 429 -> exponential backoff + jitter; circuit-breaker opens after 5 consecutive 429s for 30s. Record to telemetry as error_code=throttle.
- KV cache eviction thrash: high token counts causing OOM -> add default max_cache_entries=2048 and fallback to direct call with small batch size.
- Partial streaming: mid-stream error -> return partial response with flag partial=true, log stack and sample of prompt to restricted telemetry bucket.

Rollout checklist (canary gating):
- Pre-canary: run synthetic workload matching real traffic (seq length distribution) in sandbox for 48h.
- Canary (5%): observe 15m sliding window for latency/cost anomalies, SLO: p99 < 800ms for short prompts.
- Auto-rollback triggers: >2x baseline tokens-per-request or >3% error-rate increase sustained for 10m.

Open questions (to resolve during next sprint):
- Do we default to cached embeddings for ’semantic search’ routes? (tradeoff: freshness vs cost).
- Which telemetry fields are PII-sensitive? need legal review for prompt snippets in error logs.
- Is 30d detailed retention acceptable for compliance customers? (option toggle required).

Notes from experiments (quick hits):
- Diego: stubbed devkit reduces first-request time from ~46m to ~12m in our internal trials (n=7 teams).
- Priya: defaulting to 10k ms client timeout hides cold-starts; prefer 5s for short LLM calls and a specific route override.
- Samir: including cost-estimate meter in telemetry helped one team avoid a $3k surprise on low-traffic but high-token workloads.

Next steps (actionable):
- [ ] capture a 15min video walkthrough + annotated GitHub example by EOD next Wed (owner: Maya).
- [ ] PR: add docker devkit with scaffolding + mock ingest endpoint (owner: Diego). GH link placeholder: ENG-PR-1372.
- [ ] legal: quick check on prompt snippets and redaction defaults (owner: Priya).
- [ ] UX: tiny onboarding modal content for Console linking to this kit (owner: Samir).

Slack threads and refs:
- #sdk-onramp: initial trial notes
- #devexp: prototype demo scheduled Thu 10am PT

Unresolved UX roughs (brain dump):
- onboarding modal should show: estimated cost per 1k tokens, sample p50 latency, one click to provision sandbox key.
- single-file quickstart (index.js/python) to reduce confusion—language toggles but same minimal flow.

If you pick this up: start with "run-local.sh" in the repo scaffold, open the telemetry ingest on port 8081, and spin the synthetic generator with --profile=short. Keep notes here.

-- end of scratchbook --
